cues.en: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues is one of those topics that a lot of students find particularly unintuitive. Questions like why are we doing this and what does this actually mean are too often left just floating away in an unanswered sea of computations. And as I've put out the videos of this series, a lot of you have commented about looking forward to visualizing this topic in particular. I suspect that the reason for this is not so much that eigen things are particularly complicated or poorly explained.
cues.zh: 特征向量和特征值是很多学生觉得特别反直觉的话题之一。诸如“我们为什么要学这个”和“这到底代表什么”这类问题，往往被淹没在海量的机械计算中，得不到解答。随着本系列视频的发布，很多人也留言说，特别期待能将这个主题可视化。我觉得原因倒不在于特征相关的知识特别复杂，或者解释得不够好。

cues.en: In fact, it's comparatively straightforward, and I think most books do a fine job explaining it. The issue is that it only really makes sense if you have a solid visual understanding for many of the topics that precede it. Most important here is that you know how to think about matrices as linear transformations, but you also need to be comfortable with things like determinants, linear systems of equations, and change of basis.
cues.zh: 事实上，它相对直观，我觉得大多数教材在这点上也解释得不错。问题在于，只有对它前面涉及的诸多内容建立起扎实的直观理解，它才真正讲得通。其中最核心的，是你得知道如何把矩阵看作线性变换，但同时你也得熟悉行列式、线性方程组和基变换等概念。

cues.en: Confusion about eigenstuffs usually has more to do with the shaky foundation in one of these topics than it does with eigenvectors and eigenvalues themselves. To start, consider some linear transformation in two dimensions, like the one shown here. It moves the basis vector i-hat to the coordinates 3,0 and j-hat to 1,2. So it's represented with a matrix whose columns are 3,0 and 1,2. Focus in on what it does to one particular vector.
cues.zh: 对特征概念感到困惑，通常是因为对这些前置知识掌握不牢，而不是特征向量和特征值本身的问题。首先，来看一个二维平面上的线性变换，比如画面展示的这个。它把基向量 i-hat 变换到坐标 (3, 0)，把 j-hat 变换到 (1, 2)。因此它可以用一个列向量分别为 (3, 0) 和 (1, 2) 的矩阵来表示。现在，重点观察它对某个特定向量做了什么。

cues.en: And think about the span of that vector, the line passing through its origin and its tip. Most vectors are going to get knocked off their span during the transformation. I mean, it would seem pretty coincidental if the place where the vector landed also happens to be somewhere on that line. But some special vectors do remain on their own span, meaning the effect that the matrix has on such a vector is just to stretch it or squish it, like a scalar. For this specific example, the basis vector i-hat
cues.zh: 想一想该向量张成的空间，也就是穿过原点和它尖端的那条直线。在变换过程中，大多数向量都会脱离它们原本所在的直线。毕竟，向量变换后的落点恰好还落在原本那条线上，看起来未免太巧合了。但确实存在一些特殊的向量，它们仍停留在自己张成的空间里，这意味着矩阵对这类向量的作用，仅仅是像标量一样拉伸或压缩它们。以当前这个例子来说，基向量 i-hat

cues.en: is one such special vector. The span of i-hat is the x-axis, and from the first column of the matrix, we can see that i-hat moves over to 3 times itself, still on that x-axis. What's more, because of the way linear transformations work, any other vector on the x-axis is also just stretched by a factor of 3, and hence remains on its own span. A slightly sneakier vector that remains on its own span during this transformation is negative 1, 1.
cues.zh: 就是这样一个特殊的向量。i-hat 张成的空间就是 x 轴，从矩阵的第一列我们可以看出，i-hat 变成了原本的 3 倍，而且依然落在 x 轴上。更重要的是，基于线性变换的特性，x 轴上的任何其他向量也都会被拉伸为原来的 3 倍，因此都保留在各自张成的空间中。在这个变换下，还有一个稍微隐蔽一点、能留在原本直线上的向量，那就是 (-1, 1)。

cues.en: It ends up getting stretched by a factor of 2. And again, linearity is going to imply that any other vector on the diagonal line spanned by this guy is just going to get stretched out by a factor of 2. And for this transformation, those are all the vectors with this special property of staying on their span. Those on the x-axis getting stretched out by a factor of 3, and those on this diagonal line getting stretched by a factor of 2.
cues.zh: 它最终被拉伸为原来的 2 倍。同样，线性性质意味着，由这个向量张成的对角线上的任何其他向量，也都会被拉伸为原来的 2 倍。对于这个变换而言，具备“保留在自身张成空间中”这一特性的，就只有这些向量了。x 轴上的向量被拉伸了 3 倍，而这条对角线上的向量则被拉伸了 2 倍。

cues.en: Any other vector is going to get rotated somewhat during the transformation, knocked off the line that it spans. As you might have guessed by now, these special vectors are called the eigenvectors of the transformation. And each eigenvector has associated with it what's called an eigenvalue, which is just the factor by which it's stretched or squished during the transformation. Of course, there's nothing special about stretching versus squishing, or the fact that these eigenvalues happen to be positive.
cues.zh: 其他向量都会在变换中受到一定旋转，被撞离它张成的直线。你可能已经猜到了，这些特殊向量叫作该变换的特征向量。每个特征向量都有一个对应的特征值，也就是它在变换中被拉伸或压缩的倍数。当然，拉伸和压缩本身没什么特别，这些特征值恰好为正也没什么特别。

cues.en: In another example, you could have an eigenvector with eigenvalue negative one half, meaning that the vector gets flipped and squished by a factor of one half. But the important part here is that it stays on the line that it spans out without getting rotated off of it. For a glimpse of why this might be a useful thing to think about, consider some three-dimensional rotation. If you can find an eigenvector for that rotation, a vector that remains on its own span, what you have found
cues.zh: 再看一个例子，你可以有一个特征向量，其特征值为负二分之一，意思是这个向量被翻转，并按二分之一压缩。但关键在于，它仍留在自己张成的直线上，不会被旋转出去。想初步了解为什么这值得思考，可以想想某个三维旋转。如果你能找出那个旋转的一个特征向量——一个仍留在自身张成空间中的向量，那么你找到的

cues.en: is the axis of rotation. And it's much easier to think about a 3D rotation in terms of some axis of rotation and an angle by which it's rotating, rather than thinking about the full 3x3 matrix associated with that transformation. In this case, by the way, the corresponding eigenvalue would have to be 1, since rotations never stretch or squish anything, so the length of the vector would remain the same. This pattern shows up a lot in linear algebra.
cues.zh: 就是旋转轴。而且，用旋转轴和旋转角度来理解三维旋转，要比考虑与该变换关联的完整3×3矩阵容易得多。顺便说，这种情况下对应的特征值必须是1，因为旋转从不拉伸或压缩任何东西，所以向量的长度保持不变。这种模式在线性代数中经常出现。

cues.en: With any linear transformation described by a matrix, you could understand what it's doing by reading off the columns of this matrix as the landing spots for basis vectors. But often, a better way to get at the heart of what the linear transformation actually does, less dependent on your particular coordinate system, is to find the eigenvectors and eigenvalues.
cues.zh: 对于任何由矩阵描述的线性变换，你可以把矩阵的列读作基向量的落点，从而理解它在做什么。但通常，想抓住线性变换实际作用的核心，又不那么依赖你特定的坐标系，更好的办法是求特征向量和特征值。

cues.en: I won't cover the full details on methods for computing eigenvectors and eigenvalues here, but I'll try to give an overview of the computational ideas that are most important for a conceptual understanding. Symbolically, here's what the idea of an eigenvector looks like. A is the matrix representing some transformation, with V as the eigenvector, and lambda is a number, namely the corresponding eigenvalue. What this expression is saying is that the matrix vector product, A times V,
cues.zh: 这里我不会展开计算特征向量和特征值的全部方法细节，但会概述对概念理解最重要的计算思想。用符号表示，特征向量的概念长这样。A 是表示某个变换的矩阵，V 是特征向量，lambda 是一个数，即对应的特征值。这个表达式说的是，矩阵向量乘积 A 乘以 V，

cues.en: gives the same result as just scaling the eigenvector V by some value lambda. So finding the eigenvectors and their eigenvalues of a matrix A comes down to finding the values of V and lambda that make this expression true. It's a little awkward to work with at first because that left-hand side represents matrix vector multiplication, but the right-hand side here is scalar vector multiplication. So let's start by rewriting that right-hand side as some kind of matrix vector multiplication.
cues.zh: 得到的结果，与只用某个值 lambda 缩放特征向量 V 相同。所以，求矩阵 A 的特征向量及其特征值，就归结为找到让这个表达式成立的 V 和 lambda 的值。一开始操作起来有点别扭，因为左边表示矩阵向量乘法，而右边是标量乘向量。所以我们先把右边改写成某种矩阵向量乘法。

cues.en: using a matrix which has the effect of scaling any vector by a factor of lambda. The columns of such a matrix will represent what happens to each basis vector, and each basis vector is simply multiplied by lambda, so this matrix will have the number lambda down the diagonal with zeros everywhere else. The common way to write this guy is to factor that lambda out and write it as lambda times i, where i is the identity matrix with ones down the diagonal.
cues.zh: 可以使用一个能把任意向量缩放 lambda 倍的矩阵。这种矩阵的各列代表每个基向量的变化，由于每个基向量都只是乘上了 lambda，所以该矩阵对角线上全都是 lambda，其余位置全为零。通常的写法是把 lambda 提出来，写成 lambda 乘以 I，这里的 I 是对角线全为 1 的单位矩阵。

cues.en: With both sides looking like matrix vector multiplication, we can subtract off that right-hand side and factor out the V. So what we now have is a new matrix, A minus lambda times the identity, and we're looking for a vector V such that this new matrix times V gives the zero vector. Now, this will always be true if V itself is the zero vector, but that's boring. What we want is a non-zero eigenvector.
cues.zh: 现在等式两边都是矩阵与向量的乘积了，我们把右边项减过来，并把 v 提出来。这样我们就得到了一个新矩阵：A 减去 lambda 乘以单位矩阵，而我们找的就是一个向量 v，让这个新矩阵乘以 v 等于零向量。当然，如果 v 本身就是零向量，这永远成立，但这太无聊了。我们想要的是非零特征向量。

cues.en: And if you watch chapter 5 and 6, you'll know that the only way it's possible for the product of a matrix with a non-zero vector to become zero is if the transformation associated with that matrix squishes space into a lower dimension. And that squishification corresponds to a zero determinant for the matrix. To be concrete, let's say your matrix A has columns 2, 1, and 2, 3.
cues.zh: 如果你看过第 5 章和第 6 章就会知道，矩阵和一个非零向量相乘能得到零向量的唯一可能，就是该矩阵对应的变换把空间压缩到了更低的维度。而这种维度的压缩，对应着该矩阵的行列式为零。具体来说，假设你的矩阵 A 的列向量是 (2, 1) 和 (2, 3)。

cues.en: and think about subtracting off a variable amount, lambda, from each diagonal entry. Now imagine tweaking lambda, turning a knob to change its value. As that value of lambda changes, the matrix itself changes, and so the determinant of the matrix changes. The goal here is to find a value of lambda that will make this determinant zero, meaning the tweaked transformation squishes space into a lower dimension.
cues.zh: 设想从对角线的每个元素中减去一个变量 lambda。现在想象去调节 lambda，像转动旋钮一样改变它的值。随着 lambda 的变化，矩阵本身在变，矩阵的行列式也随之改变。这里的目标是找到一个能让行列式为零的 lambda 值，这意味着调整后的变换把空间压缩到了更低维度。

cues.en: In this case, the sweet spot comes when lambda equals 1. Of course, if we had chosen some other matrix, the eigenvalue might not necessarily be 1. The sweet spot might be hit at some other value of lambda. So this is kind of a lot, but let's unravel what this is saying. When lambda equals 1, the matrix A minus lambda times the identity squishes space onto a line. That means there's a non-zero vector V such that A minus lambda times the identity times V
cues.zh: 在这个例子中，最佳取值是当 lambda 等于 1 的时候。当然，如果选的是其他矩阵，特征值就不一定是 1，最佳取值可能会出现在 lambda 的其他值上。信息量可能有点大，但我们来梳理一下它的含义。当 lambda 等于 1 时，矩阵 A 减去 lambda 乘以单位矩阵会把空间压缩成一条直线。这意味着存在一个非零向量 v，使得 A 减去 lambda 乘以单位矩阵再乘以 v

cues.en: equals the zero vector. And remember, the reason we care about that is because it means a times v equals lambda times v, which you can read off as saying that the vector v is an eigenvector of a, staying on its own span during the transformation a. In this example, the corresponding eigenvalue is 1, so v would actually just stay fixed in place. Pause and ponder if you need to make sure that that line of reasoning feels good.
cues.zh: 等于零向量。别忘了，我们之所以关心这个，是因为它意味着 A 乘以 v 等于 lambda 乘以 v，这代表向量 v 是 A 的一个特征向量，在变换 A 期间保持在自身张成的空间中。在这个例子里，对应的特征值是 1，所以 v 实际上根本没有改变位置。如果需要的话，可以暂停思考一下，确保这一连串推导逻辑顺畅。

cues.en: This is the kind of thing I mentioned in the introduction. If you didn't have a solid grasp of determinants and why they relate to linear systems of equations having non-zero solutions, an expression like this would feel completely out of the blue. To see this in action, let's revisit the example from the start, with a matrix whose columns are 3, 0, and 1, 2. To find if a value lambda is an eigenvalue, subtract it from the diagonals of this matrix and compute the determinant.
cues.zh: 这就是我在开头提到的那种情况。如果你没有扎实掌握行列式，以及它为什么和线性方程组有非零解有关，那像这样的表达式会让你觉得完全摸不着头脑。为了看看实际是怎么回事，让我们回到开头的例子，矩阵的列是 3、0 和 1、2。要判断某个值 lambda 是不是特征值，把它从矩阵的对角线上减去，然后计算行列式。

cues.en: Doing this, we get a certain quadratic polynomial in lambda, 3 minus lambda times 2 minus lambda. Since lambda can only be an eigenvalue if this determinant happens to be 0, you can conclude that the only possible eigenvalues are lambda equals 2 and lambda equals 3. To figure out what the eigenvectors are that actually have one of these eigenvalues, say lambda equals 2, plug in that value of lambda to the matrix,
cues.zh: 这样做，我们得到一个关于 lambda 的二次多项式，(3 减 lambda) 乘以 (2 减 lambda)。由于只有当这个行列式恰好为 0 时 lambda 才可能是特征值，你可以得出结论：唯一可能的特征值是 lambda 等于 2 和 lambda 等于 3。要想知道真正具有这些特征值之一（比如 lambda 等于 2）的特征向量是什么，把那个 lambda 值代入矩阵，

cues.en: and then solve for which vectors this diagonally altered matrix sends to 0. If you computed this the way you would any other linear system, you'd see that the solutions are all the vectors on the diagonal line spanned by negative 1, 1. This corresponds to the fact that the unaltered matrix, 3, 0, 1, 2, has the effect of stretching all those vectors by a factor of 2. Now, a 2D transformation doesn't have to have eigenvectors.
cues.zh: 然后求解这个对角线被改动后的矩阵把哪些向量映射到 0。如果你像处理任何其他线性方程组那样计算，你会看到解就是由 (-1, 1) 张成的对角线上的所有向量。这对应于一个事实：未改动的矩阵 3、0、1、2 的效果是把所有这些向量拉伸 2 倍。不过，二维变换不一定有特征向量。

cues.en: For example, consider a rotation by 90 degrees. This doesn't have any eigenvectors, since it rotates every vector off of its own span. If you actually try computing the eigenvalues of a rotation like this, notice what happens. Its matrix has columns 0, 1 and negative 1, 0. Subtract off lambda from the diagonal elements and look for when the determinant is 0. In this case, you get the polynomial lambda squared plus 1.
cues.zh: 例如，考虑旋转 90 度。它没有任何特征向量，因为它把每个向量都旋转到它自己张成的直线之外。如果你真的尝试计算这种旋转的特征值，注意会发生什么。它的矩阵的列是 0、1 和 -1、0。从对角线元素中减去 lambda，然后看行列式什么时候为 0。在这种情况下，你得到多项式 lambda 的平方加 1。

cues.en: The only roots of that polynomial are the imaginary numbers, i and negative i. The fact that there are no real number solutions indicates that there are no eigenvectors. Another pretty interesting example worth holding in the back of your mind is a shear. This fixes i-hat in place and moves j-hat 1 over, so its matrix has columns 1, 0 and 1, 1. All of the vectors on the x-axis are eigenvectors with eigenvalue 1.
cues.zh: 那个多项式唯一的根是虚数 i 和 -i。没有实数解这一事实说明没有特征向量。另一个相当有趣、值得记在心里的例子是剪切。它把 i-hat 固定不动，把 j-hat 移动 1 格，所以它的矩阵的列是 1、0 和 1、1。x 轴上的所有向量都是特征值为 1 的特征向量，

cues.en: since they remain fixed in place. In fact, these are the only eigenvectors. When you subtract off lambda from the diagonals and compute the determinant, what you get is 1 minus lambda squared. And the only root of this expression is lambda equals 1. This lines up with what we see geometrically, that all of the eigenvectors have eigenvalue 1. Keep in mind though, it's also possible to have just one eigenvalue
cues.zh: 因为它们保持不动。事实上，这些就是唯一的特征向量。当你从对角线上减去 lambda 并计算行列式时，得到的是 (1 减 lambda) 的平方。这个表达式唯一的根是 lambda 等于 1。这与我们从几何上看到的一致：所有特征向量的特征值都是 1。不过要记住，也有可能只有一个特征值，

cues.en: but with more than just a line full of eigenvectors. A simple example is a matrix that scales everything by 2. The only eigenvalue is 2, but every vector in the plane gets to be an eigenvector with that eigenvalue. Now is another good time to pause and ponder some of this before I move on to the last topic. I want to finish off here with the idea of an eigenbasis, which relies heavily on ideas from the last video.
cues.zh: 但它对应的特征向量不止一条直线那么多。一个简单的例子是把所有东西都缩放 2 倍的矩阵。唯一的特征值是 2，但平面上的每个向量都可以是特征值为 2 的特征向量。现在是另一个好时机，停下来思考一下这些内容，然后再进入最后一个话题。我想用特征基这个概念来收尾，它很大程度上依赖于上一个视频里的想法。

cues.en: Take a look at what happens if our basis vectors just so happen to be eigenvectors. For example, maybe i-hat is scaled by negative 1 and j-hat is scaled by 2. Writing their new coordinates as the columns of a matrix, notice that those scalar multiples, negative 1 and 2, which are the eigenvalues of i-hat and j-hat, sit on the diagonal of our matrix, and every other entry is a zero.
cues.zh: 看看如果我们的基向量刚好就是特征向量，会发生什么。举个例子，比如 i-hat 被缩放了 -1 倍，j-hat 被缩放了 2 倍。把它们变换后的新坐标写成矩阵的列向量，你会发现，这两个缩放倍数，也就是 i-hat 和 j-hat 的特征值 -1 和 2，刚好坐落在矩阵的主对角线上，而其他所有元素全都是零。

cues.en: Any time a matrix has zeros everywhere other than the diagonal, it's called, reasonably enough, a diagonal matrix. And the way to interpret this is that all the basis vectors are eigenvectors, with the diagonal entries of this matrix being their eigenvalues. There are a lot of things that make diagonal matrices much nicer to work with. One big one is that it's easier to compute what will happen if you multiply this matrix by itself a whole bunch of times.
cues.zh: 只要一个矩阵除了对角线以外其他位置全是零，它就很自然地被称为对角矩阵。理解它的方式就是：所有的基向量都是特征向量，而矩阵对角线上的元素就是它们对应的特征值。处理对角矩阵有很多非常爽的地方。其中一个巨大的优势就是，如果你想把这个矩阵自乘很多很多次，算起来会极其容易。

cues.en: Since all one of these matrices does is scale each basis vector by some eigenvalue, applying that matrix many times, say 100 times, is just going to correspond to scaling each basis vector by the 100th power of the corresponding eigenvalue. In contrast, try computing the 100th power of a non-diagonal matrix. Really, try it for a moment. It's a nightmare. Of course, you'll rarely be so lucky as to have your basis vectors also be eigenvectors.
cues.zh: 因为这种矩阵所做的，无非就是用某个特征值去缩放对应的基向量，所以连续应用这个矩阵多次，比如 100 次，就完全等同于把每个基向量缩放到对应特征值的 100 次方倍。相比之下，你试着算一下一个非对角矩阵的 100 次方看看。真的，去试一下。那简直是场噩梦。当然，你很少会有这么好的运气，能碰上基向量本身就是特征向量的情况。

cues.en: But if your transformation has a lot of eigenvectors, like the one from the start of this video, enough so that you can choose a set that spans the full space, then you could change your coordinate system so that these eigenvectors are your basis vectors. I talked about change of basis last video, but I'll go through a super quick reminder here of how to express a transformation currently written in our coordinate system into a different system. Take the coordinates of the vectors that you want to use as a new basis.
cues.zh: 但如果你的变换拥有足够多的特征向量，就像本期视频开头展示的那个一样，多到你可以挑出一组来张成整个空间，那你就可以变换坐标系，让这些特征向量充当你的基向量。我在上一期视频里讲过基变换，不过这里我可以超快速地帮大家复习一下，怎么把当前坐标系下的变换改写到另一个坐标系中。首先取你想要作为新基底的那些向量的坐标。

cues.en: which in this case means our two eigenvectors, that make those coordinates the columns of a matrix, known as the change of basis matrix. When you sandwich the original transformation, putting the change of basis matrix on its right and the inverse of the change of basis matrix on its left, the result will be a matrix representing that same transformation, but from the perspective of the new basis vector's coordinate system.
cues.zh: 在这里就是我们的那两个特征向量，把这些坐标作为列组成一个矩阵，也就是所谓的基变换矩阵。当你把原始变换“夹在中间”，右边乘上基变换矩阵，左边乘上基变换矩阵的逆矩阵时，得到的结果就是一个表示完全相同变换的矩阵，只不过它是从新基向量坐标系的角度来看的。

cues.en: The whole point of doing this with eigenvectors is that this new matrix is guaranteed to be diagonal with its corresponding eigenvalues down that diagonal. This is because it represents working in a coordinate system where what happens to the basis vectors is that they get scaled during the transformation. A set of basis vectors which are also eigenvectors is called, again reasonably enough, an eigenbasis. So if, for example, you needed to compute the 100th power of this matrix,
cues.zh: 用特征向量来做这件事的核心目的，在于这个新矩阵一定是对角矩阵，而且对角线上整整齐齐排着对应的特征值。这是因为它代表了这样一个坐标系：在变换过程中，基向量所经历的仅仅是纯粹的缩放。一组本身就是特征向量的基向量，非常合情合理地，被称为特征基。所以举个例子，如果你需要计算这个矩阵的 100 次方，

cues.en: it would be much easier to change to an eigenbasis, compute the 100th power in that system, then convert back to our standard system. You can't do this with all transformations. A shear, for example, doesn't have enough eigenvectors to span the full space. But if you can find an eigenbasis, it makes matrix operations really lovely. For those of you willing to work through a pretty neat puzzle to see what this looks like in action and how it can be used to produce some surprising results,
cues.zh: 那换到特征基下，在那个系统里算出 100 次方，然后再转换回我们的标准系统，就会容易得多。并不是所有的变换都能这么做。比如剪切变换，就没有足够的特征向量来张成整个空间。但只要你能找到一组特征基，它就会让矩阵运算变得无比美妙。对于那些愿意动脑解一道精妙难题、想看看这套操作在实际中如何发挥作用并带来惊人结果的朋友，

cues.en: I'll leave up a prompt here on the screen. It takes a bit of work, but I think you'll enjoy it. The next and final video of this series is going to be on abstract vector spaces. See you then!
cues.zh: 我会在屏幕上留下一道思考题。虽然需要花点心思，但我相信你会乐在其中的。本系列的下一期，也是最后一期视频，将深入探讨抽象向量空间。我们下期见！
